metadata.section: The Infinitesimal Model and Its Extensions: Introduction
metadata.source_title: Evolution and Selection of Quantitative Traits
metadata.section_level_1: The Infinitesimal Model and Its Extensions: Introduction
heading_path: The Infinitesimal Model and Its Extensions: Introduction

blocks.content: Both the standard infinitesimal and Gaussian COA models assume unlinked loci. When loci are linked, the contribution from gametic-phase disequilibrium, d, decays by less than half in each generation. This allows higher values to accrue, yielding a larger value of $ |d| $ at equilibrium. We examine the impact of linkage under two different settings. First, we consider the Gaussian COA approximation (requiring multivariate normality of the locus-specific distributions of effects), and second, allowing for departures from normality serves as an entry point for our final section on treating non-Gaussian distributions of genetic values.
